chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:

I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: There belonged to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) a she-camel upon which he performed hajj twenty-two times, and he never struck her with a single blow at all.

He said: Then, after his death, she came, and we were not aware of her until one of our servants, or one of the mawālī, came to me and said: The she-camel has gone out and come to the grave of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, then knelt upon it, rubbing the grave with the front of her neck while she was moaning.
So I said: Catch her, catch her, and bring her to me before they come to know of her or see her. He said: And she had never seen the grave at all.

key_terms.بِجِرَانِهَا: with the front part of her neck/chest against the ground
key_terms.تَرْغُو: she was making the sound of a camel, moaning
key_terms.حَجَّةً: a pilgrimage journey; here, one of the twenty-two hajj journeys
key_terms.قَبْرَ: the grave of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام)
key_terms.قَرَعَهَا: he struck her; here, negated to show he never hit her
key_terms.مَوْتِهِ: his death, referring to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام)
key_terms.نَاقَةٌ: a she-camel belonging to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn’s she-camel in al-Kāfī relate about his character and the sign seen after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) used a she-camel for twenty-two hajj journeys and never struck her. After his death, the animal came on its own to his grave, knelt there, and rubbed herself against it while moaning, which is presented as a remarkable sign connected to the Imam (عليه السلام).
